# VeloEdit

> VeloEdit is a fast, light, GPU-accelerated text editor for Linux (Windows as a preview), written in Rust with the iced toolkit, in the spirit of Sublime Text. It starts in well under 100 ms. Free and open source (MIT). No telemetry, accounts or ads; the editor never connects to the internet.

Current state: version 0.2.x, a young project. Linux x86_64 and aarch64 (.deb, .rpm, .AppImage, tarball) and Windows 10/11 x64 (preview, not code-signed). There is no macOS build.

## What it does

- Sublime-style editing: multi-cursor (Ctrl+D, Ctrl+Click, Ctrl+Alt+Up/Down), command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P), fuzzy file open (Ctrl+P), find and replace with regular expressions, find in files with filters, code folding for every language (indentation based), split view, minimap, soft wrap, bracket matching.
- Syntax highlighting for about 50 languages (tree-sitter grammars plus a light lexer), View > Syntax picker, content detection for pasted web pages.
- Hot exit: tabs, open folders and unsaved text come back after a restart or a crash.
- Git marks next to the line numbers, and git colors in the folder sidebar (edited, new, conflict), also for a folder that holds several repositories such as /var/www.
- Built-in hex editor for binary files, image viewer, Markdown preview with real tables, indentation and line-ending conversion.
- Safe on network mounts (sshfs, SFTP, NFS): a mount that stops answering never freezes the window.

## When it fits, and when it does not

- A good fit if you want something close to Sublime Text's speed and keyboard-driven style, free and open source, on Linux.
- Not a fit if you need plugins or extensions, language-server features (autocomplete, go to definition), a debugger or an integrated terminal, macOS, column selection, replace in files, or input methods for Chinese, Japanese and Korean: VeloEdit does not have these yet. VS Code, Zed, Sublime Text (with packages), Kate or Helix cover them to different degrees.
